reviewed_instruction_spec.task_title: Build product-summary slides from inventory JSON using template deck
reviewed_instruction_spec.information_flow: linux.json (first Linux) -> filter/transform approved products -> linux.odp_pptx template (second Linux) -> create updated ODP deck on second Linux
reviewed_instruction_spec.instruction: On the first Linux device, open the product inventory JSON at /home/user/data/products.json. On the second Linux device, open the presentation template /home/user/presentations/template.odp and create a new presentation named /home/user/presentations/product_updates.odp. For every product in the JSON whose status is "approved", add a Product Summary slide (one per approved product) using the template slide and fill the text anchors so each slide shows Product ID, Name, Version, and Status. Save the deck at the target path on the second Linux device.
reviewed_instruction_spec.detailed_description: Read the JSON inventory on the first Linux device. The JSON contains a list of product records (product_id, name, version, status). Select only records where status == "approved". On the second Linux device there is an ODP template deck containing a template slide titled "Template Slide: Product Summary" with text anchors for PRODUCT_ID, PRODUCT_NAME, VERSION, STATUS. For each approved product, create a new slide based on that template slide and populate the anchors with the product's product_id, name, version, and status. Save the resulting ODP deck as /home/user/presentations/product_updates.odp. The required output semantics: the saved deck must contain one Product Summary slide per approved product from the JSON and each such slide must include deterministic text anchors with the Product ID, Name, Version and Status values taken from the JSON. The expected_data values (product IDs, names, versions, statuses) are directly taken from the JSON source; the mapping to slides is determined by the presence of the template slide anchors in the template ODP on the second device.
reviewed_instruction_spec.why_cross_device: The product records (the authoritative data) are on the first Linux device as a JSON file, while the slide template and the final presentation must be created/updated on the second Linux device; creating per-product slides therefore requires reading data on the first device and writing the updated deck on the second device.
